newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WEST INDIES WIN TOSS, CHOOSE TO BAT V AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES WIN TOSS, CHOOSE TO BAT V AUSTRALIA.

text.p: West Indies captain Courtney Walsh won the toss and elected to bat against Australia on the first day of their fourth test match at the Adelaide Oval on Saturday.
West Indies were expected to begin the match with a psychological edge, having crushed Australia in the last test inside three days and beaten them twice in recent one-day matches.
But the last-minute replacement of strike fast bowler Curtly Ambrose, the main destroyer for the West Indies in the last test, has weakened their bowling attack.
Rookie right-arm fast bowler Patterson Thompson, who has played only one test, replaces Ambrose who failed a morning fitness test with a strained groin.
Paceman Cameron Cuffy, who has played two tests, replaces Kenny Benjamin who was forced home earlier this month with a side-strain.
Australia lead the five test series 2-1 and only need to draw or win this match to retain the Frank Worrell Trophy.
Australia, who ended West Indies' 15-year unbeaten record in 1995, began the series in commanding style with wins in Brisbane and Sydney.
But a resurgent Curtly Ambrose, transformed from the lethargic figure of the first two tests, exploded into action in the third test in Melbourne, giving West Indies victory with two days to spare.
In addition Brian Lara, seemingly unable to cope with Glenn McGrath's off-cutters in the first three tests, has scored 295 runs in the first three one-day matches of the New Year.
Australia start the match with two changes to the side that lost the Melbourne test, although they were dictated by injury rather than form.

Fast bowler Andrew Bichel replaces Stuart Gillespie who is injured with a side strain, while allrounder Michael Bevan has been elevated from 12th man at the expense of Paul Reiffel, who is returning from an injury in between the tests.

West Indies - Sherwin Campbell, Adrian Griffith, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Brian Lara, Carl Hooper, Jimmy Adams, Junior Murray, Ian Bishop, Patterson Thompson, Courtney Walsh (captain), Cameron Cuffy, Phil Simmons (12th man).
Australia - Mark Taylor (captain), Matthew Hayden, Justin Langer, Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Greg Blewett, Michael Bevan, Ian Healy, Shane Warne, Andrew Bichel, Glenn McGrath, Paul Reiffel (12th man).
